questions.q:
Predict the output:

```bash
uv init --no-package --python 3.14 poketeam
cat poketeam/.python-version
```
explanations: Right. `.python-version` holds the one Python version uv should use for this project.
`>=3.14` is the rule in `pyproject.toml` (`requires-python`). `.python-version` names a single version.
The project name goes in `pyproject.toml`, not in `.python-version`.
`uv init --python 3.14` writes `3.14` into it.

questions.q: `pyproject.toml` says `"pydantic>=2.10,<3"`. Which of these versions can uv install?
explanations: `2.9.2` is older than `2.10`, so `>=2.10` rules it out.
Right. `2.12.0` is at least `2.10` and still below `3`, so it fits both parts of the rule.
`<3` rules out version 3, the major version that's allowed to break your code.
`>=` and `<` give a range. Exactly one version would be `==2.10`.

questions.q: Which of these should be committed to the project's repository?
explanations: `.venv` is big and only works on the machine that made it. `uv sync` rebuilds it from the lock file.
`.venv` is exactly the part that shouldn't be committed.
Right. The recipe and the receipt get committed, and every machine builds its own `.venv` from them.
Without `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock`, a teammate can't rebuild the same environment.
Exactly 0.28.1 would be `==0.28.1`. The exact version you got is recorded in `uv.lock`.
Right. `>=` sets the lowest version allowed. The lock file records which one was actually installed.
`>=` is "at least", so older versions are ruled out.
There's a lower limit: nothing older than 0.28.1.

questions.q: `main.py` starts with `import httpx`. `python3 main.py` fails with `No module named 'httpx'`, but `uv run main.py` works. Why?
options: `python3` is Ubuntu's own Python, which doesn't have the project's packages
uv deletes httpx when you're not using it
explanations: It's installed, in the project's `.venv`. That's why `uv run` works.
Right. `uv run` uses the project's Python and packages. Plain `python3` uses the system's, which has none of them.
The same file works with `uv run`, so the code is fine.
The packages stay in `.venv` until you remove them.
